title: Information abundance is separating access from trust while platform accountability and AI-mediated search reshape the conditions for shared reality
source_unit: International Panel on the Information Environment, Trends in the Information Environment: 2026 Expert Survey Results
geography: 71 countries of expertise, including developed and developing economies and a separately reported United States comparison

observations.period: May-June 2026; expert outlook on information-environment conditions

denominator.unit: experts studying information environments across 71 countries

expected_worsening.unit: percent expecting the information environment in their country of expertise to worsen over the following year

trend_comparison.value: expected worsening rose from 53% in 2023 to 76% in 2026

developing_country_information_access.unit: percent of experts on developing economies saying people have the information needed to participate in civic life

observations.method: Fourth annual IPIE expert survey conducted 6 May-8 June 2026; researchers were recruited through academic databases, professional networks, nominations, and targeted outreach, with 470 completed responses representing 71 countries of expertise.
observations.uncertainty: This is a partly self-selected expert sample and a repeated cross-section, not a probability sample of publics or experts, a behavioral trace, or a causal forecast; the outlook question also combines direction and confidence and may elicit expert pessimism.
observations.subgroup: Researchers studying developed economies, developing economies, and the United States; nearly half of respondents focused on developing economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Expert pessimism can rise because measurement and awareness improve; information access, civic participation, and institutional trust can also differ sharply within countries.

observations.period: 2026; access, trust, and the quality of online information

denominator.unit: IPIE experts in the analytic sample

diverse_viewpoints_access.unit: percent saying people can find diverse viewpoints online at least somewhat easily

mainstream_news_trust.unit: percent believing most people in their country trust mainstream news outlets to report politics accurately

platform_accountability_threat.unit: percent rating lack of platform accountability a big or extreme threat

misinformation_threat.unit: percent rating misinformation a big or extreme threat

access_trust_gap.value: people may encounter many viewpoints without having confidence that the information is accurate or accountable

observations.method: Expert ratings of healthy-information features, threats, online viewpoint access, and public trust in political reporting, with percentages calculated over all 470 respondents including don’t-know responses in the denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Expert judgments do not measure actual exposure, comprehension, news use, platform behavior, or public trust directly; threat ratings are not causal effect estimates.
observations.subgroup: Experts on information environments across country and development contexts, with developing-economy experts reporting lower confidence in distinguishing accurate from false information.
observations.counterinterpretation: Viewpoint diversity can support pluralism even when trust is low, and low trust may reflect healthy skepticism rather than only information degradation.

observations.period: 2026; AI summaries in search and information-production sustainability

denominator.unit: IPIE experts in the analytic sample

faster_answer_access.unit: percent expecting AI summaries in search results to help people find answers faster

news_traffic_reduction.unit: percent expecting AI summaries to reduce traffic to news websites

viewpoint_narrowing.unit: percent expecting AI summaries to narrow the range of viewpoints encountered

search_tradeoff.value: convenience can increase answer speed while weakening the referral, revenue, and plural-source pathways that sustain original reporting

observations.method: New IPIE questionnaire items on AI summaries in search, interpreted alongside expert views of search engines, generative AI, platforms, and news ecosystems.
observations.uncertainty: These are expectations rather than observed traffic or viewpoint effects; the survey does not distinguish all search-summary implementations or identify the causal size of any revenue or pluralism change.
observations.subgroup: Experts studying digital platforms, news, search, generative AI, misinformation, and civic information across 71 countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI summaries may reduce search friction, improve accessibility, and direct users to better sources in some contexts; original publishers may develop new funding or distribution models.

observations.period: 2026; research capacity and governance of the information environment

denominator.unit: IPIE experts in the analytic sample

funding_barrier.unit: percent citing research funding as a barrier to studying the information environment

data_access_barrier.unit: percent citing restricted data access as a barrier

government_agenda_pressure.unit: percent reporting efforts to align research with a government agenda, up from 21% in 2025

research_censorship.unit: percent reporting government censorship, more than double the 2025 share

knowledge-governance_route.value: the capacity to study and govern the information environment is itself exposed to funding, data, political-pressure, and censorship constraints

observations.method: Repeated IPIE expert survey items on research conditions, with separate comparison for experts whose country of expertise is the United States.
observations.uncertainty: Reported research pressures are expert perceptions and do not provide a census of funding cancellations, censorship events, or research quality; year-to-year differences are not panel estimates.
observations.subgroup: Information-environment researchers, including academic, nonprofit, government, media, private-sector, and independent experts; U.S.-focused experts reported elevated political and funding pressure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Research constraints can reflect ordinary competition, security, privacy, or data-protection requirements rather than censorship; political pressure reports may be sensitive to field composition.

related_sources.claim: Official IPIE summary of the 2026 expert-survey findings.

boundary: This record adds an information-environment route from platform accountability, source trust, AI-mediated search, viewpoint diversity, research capacity, and political pressure through shared reality and civic participation. It uses expert survey judgments and report synthesis, not a public prevalence estimate, observed platform traffic, direct misinformation exposure, causal political effects, or proof that AI summaries will narrow viewpoints everywhere.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IPIE publication page, press release, and 2026 synthesis report PDF reviewed for sample frame, trend comparisons, platform-accountability and misinformation threats, trust/access gap, AI-search trade-offs, and research-capacity constraints.
